title: Training-intensity Distribution on Middle- and Long-distance Runners: A Systematic Review
authors: Campos Y, Casado A, Vieira JG, Guimaraes M, et al.
findings: 20 articles identified; quantification methods (session RPE, heart rate, blood lactate, race pace, running speed) gave different zone proportions for the same training.
Studies using greater volumes of low-intensity training (pyramidal or polarized) reported larger endurance improvements than threshold TID.

Authors conclude high volume at low intensity (>=70% of overall volume) plus low volume at threshold and high-intensity interval training (<=30%) appears necessary to optimise adaptations in middle- and long-distance runners.
Authors recommend monitoring TID with both objective and subjective methods.
limitations: Heterogeneous mostly small studies; the 70/30 split is the authors' synthesis and not a pooled estimate.
implications: Use >=70% low-intensity as the hard floor and about 80% as the default (see rule tid-low-intensity-floor).
Track TID with more than one method (HR or pace time-in-zone plus session RPE).

verification.notes: Added by verifier. Crossref: online 2021-11-08, print 2022-04, vol 43; 10 authors, first four Campos, Casado, Vieira, Guimaraes, so 'et al.' used. Claims confirmed in abstract.
